paragraphs: (Baruch ben Neriah—[Jeremiah 32:12](https://www.sefaria.org/Jeremiah.32.12).) Rav Nachman bar Baruch—[Shabbat 66b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.66b.7); Nechemyah bar Baruch—[Moed Katan 16a](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.16a.11). Hyman identifies them as one person, reporting that Dikdukei Soferim also reads Nechemyah bar Baruch in [Shabbat 66b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.66b.7). In [Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 4:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Taanit.4.5.12), Rabbi Yehudah son of Rabbi Ilai says, “Baruch Rabbi used to expound.” Hyman suggests a printing error, since he finds no Tanna of that name elsewhere. He proposes that it means that he blessed his teacher when mentioning him.[^1]

notes.text: The chains also differ at Ashi bar Avin and Chiyya bar Avin. [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2688&lang=en) records both and suspects an error in one. The consulted Yerushalmi has “Baruch Rabbi.” Hyman proposes taking the first word as a blessing of the teacher.
